fixture.note: Explicit density fixture adds normal enemies through spawnEnemy and preserves initial enemies, spawnClock, HP, speed, AI, damage and normal subsequent spawning. Existing Continue/preload/resume UI launches the memory-only checkpoint.

native.note: Original native texture submission and shader API readiness before launch; not GPU completion, measured FPS or first-draw validation. A maximum of three original enemy models is owned until adoption.

playerDeferredRead.note: QA-only successful native-Canvas path; the original player module is unchanged. The full same-folder candidate only relocates the original direct/legacy read and bounds/core block after armed rendering and colour composition, before metadata/frame spreads. The installer permits the candidate only when both own directAlphaReadback and verifyAlphaReadback flags are false; direct use of the candidate class is unsupported. Direct/verification modes, custom methods and changed owners use the whole original raster. Successful colour/body/bounds/contour equivalence requires separate actual quality evidence. Universal exception/order equivalence is not claimed: a deferred body-read error follows armed/compositor work, and an armed/compositor error can occur before that read. An already-started candidate is never retried through the original. Critical Canvas methods and ink write accessors are checked without invoking custom getters. Mutation of global ImageData/HTMLCanvas accessors or Three render-graph prototypes/callbacks is outside this native-successful-path contract. Original owned assets/scene callbacks must not mutate the frozen body canvas during the call; no per-frame whole-scene traversal certifies arbitrary foreign callbacks. No clocks, poses, skins, model data, assets or saves are advanced here. verify=true is quality-only Aoriginal/Bdeferred/Aoriginal, with six GL renders instead of two plus six explicit native Canvas captures; it returns the final original output and is never a performance pass. Whole-scene A/A quality gates remain independent. Source FNV guards are consumer guards, not cryptographic provenance. No caller GPU or asset resource is owned or disposed.

performance.note: Predeclared before measurement: total preparation+40callbacks+finalDrain at least3% lower than fasterA; first callback and all four steady30 callback median/p95/max/sum no worse than eitherA, plus40/41 p95/max no worse. Native success-path quality, literal Game, usage without fallbacks, cleanup and strict whole AA/AB/BA are required. Same original fullRGBA read and original GL draw count remain. Single bracket is diagnostic, injected tests never accepted, no automatic adoption/FPS/memory claim.

drain.note: Event-driven QA-owned cleanup bookkeeping only. Register each owned Promise before wait, or synchronously/asynchronously within a retirement that has not yet completed. Promise/thenable identity is deduplicated across this tracker: only its first accepted retirement runs. A fulfilled/rejected producer is not complete until its retirement (including any returned Promise and newly registered followers) finishes. Producer rejection alone is not a cleanup failure. Capacity is a lifetime entry bound, including completed entries; rejected capacity registrations are not observed and remain the caller's cleanup responsibility. The first wait uses one overall deadline with no polling and returns one fixed immutable report. Timeout does not cancel producer/retirement Promises; already accepted and later capacity-eligible followers continue best-effort, and later snapshots may differ from that fixed wait result. Work registered after an already completed wait cannot retroactively change its result. Reports retain primitive labels/status only, not values, raw errors, resources or Promises. This tracker performs no rendering, Game, storage or GPU operation.

note: Explicit own-data playerDeferredRead:true and boundedOwnedCleanup:true, exact qa-player-deferred-read=1 and qa-owned-cleanup=1, without verify/readback-probe modes: the same original/deferred/original cost harness and strict original criteria, with one15second event-driven late-load retirement drain AFTER all preparation/callback/readback timings. Drain timing and resource resnapshot are separate and excluded from the performance numerator/denominator; native retirement callbacks may still run during later arm preparation as in the existing harness. No additional R1/floor/R2 or same-frame verification reads/draws, no profiler, new prime or extra Game tick. Complete tracked retirement and final owner/resource gates are mandatory; timeout/errors preserve a frozen failed cleanup report. Passing cost criteria is diagnostic only and does not adopt a product change or prove FPS/peak memory. Explicit own-data playerDeferredRead:true and qa-player-deferred-read=1: fresh owned unprimed original/deferred/original player arms, no GPU pass or new textures. B relocates only the original body Canvas fullRGBA read and pure bounds/core calculations to after armed GL rendering and colour Canvas composition, before metadata getters. The unchanged pre-weapon bodyCanvas snapshot supplies original RGBA and contour. This changes readback scheduling, not frame count or animation. Direct/verify and unsupported or replaced methods fall back to original and block acceptance. Successful native Canvas paths are the scope; native read failures can occur after more drawing in B, so universal exceptional side-effect ordering is not certified. All work and installer reporting stay inside callbacks. Predeclared total preparation+40callbacks+finalDrain must improve3%; first callback, steady30 median/p95/max/sum and40/41 p95/max must not regress against either original. Strict whole AA/AB/BA, literal Game and ownership cleanup remain required. Verify-only mode adds same-context original/candidate/original raster draws at each already-computed frozen pose and strict fullcolour/bodyRGBA/metadata comparison; no ticks or selection calls are added. These extra reads/draws make its timing ineligible as performance evidence; it cannot override the separate final wholeCanvas gate. No default adoption, FPS or peak-memory claim. 8851 genuine-memory QA only. Fresh owned Renderer/Art/native player and initial max-three-model NPC preparation per original/manual/original arm. Original on-demand species loads remain enabled; actual runtime model/pending maxima are reported. Main ready records are borrowed by identity and never loaded, masked or released through a mutating path. Forty fixed .12-second catch-up callbacks include their first draw; batch-eight rAF yields are reported separately. This is a renderer combat harness without app HUD, audio or persistence, not presented FPS. Certification and lifecycle wrappers are inside render timing in every arm; no Canvas-stage, native-stage or frame-cost observer is installed. Literal per-frame checkpoint/effects/motion/commands/events and both RNG states are compared outside timers. Final whole-canvas readback and PNG export follow the measured loop. Existing twelve-state/two-selected-cell pixel QA is separate evidence, not proof for every source frame. Shared URL decode caches and the live product caches remain resident; fresh instances do not imply cold driver/URL caches. Owned native pending promises are followed through late success/failure for retirement. A failed player Promise.all can have unobservable sibling requests; that failure is explicitly cleanup-unproven rather than called complete. Timings are CPU call wall, not GPU duration or peak memory. No product optimization is adopted by this utility.

readbackStorage.note: Three sequential final-canvas readback arrays and at most three PNG strings are retained until comparison, then raw arrays are dropped; source-pixel storage only, not a peak-memory measurement.
